headings.text: miniwerk: Let's Encrypt for the public plane

blocks.html:
This page describes the certificate machinery of the legacy Docker Compose stack (pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration): how CFSSL acts as the deployment's private certificate authority and how miniwerk fetches the public Let's Encrypt certificates. On the Kubernetes platform this entire subsystem is replaced — see PKI & trust for the counterpart.

Two certificate planes

The legacy stack runs two separate certificate planes:

Plane Issuer What it secures Where the material lives
Public TLS Let's Encrypt (via miniwerk + certbot) Server certificates for the browser-facing hostnames: <domain>, mtls.<domain>, tak.<domain>, kc.<domain>, etc. le_certs volume (/le_certs/rasenmaeher/fullchain.pem + privkey.pem)
Internal CA CFSSL (cfssl service) End-user client certificates (mTLS login, CN = callsign) and product service certificates cfssl_data volume (CA keys + cert DB); public parts exported to the ca_public volume

Browsers never see the internal CA on the server side — they connect to hosts presenting a Let's Encrypt certificate. The internal CA only appears on the client side of the handshake: nginx verifies presented client certificates against /ca_public/ca_chain.pem. Conversely, Let's Encrypt never signs anything used for client authentication. The diagram below shows both planes and where they meet.

blocks.html:
CFSSL: the internal CA

The internal CA is three containers built from the same cfssl/ context with different build targets (image tags shown at the compose default RELEASE_TAG 2.9.0):

Service Image Port Role
cfssl pvarki/cfssl:api-1.2.0_260427-d2.9.0 8888 cfssl serve — the signing API, signs with the intermediate CA
ocsp pvarki/cfssl:ocsp-1.2.0_260427-d2.9.0 8889 cfssl ocspserve — serves pre-signed OCSP responses from the shared cert DB
ocsprest pvarki/cfssl:ocsprest-1.0.7_260427-d2.9.0 8887 FastAPI helper wrapping the cfssl CLI: /api/v1/csr/sign, /api/v1/ocsp/sign, /api/v1/refresh, CRL dumps

On first start, cfssl-init.sh builds a two-level hierarchy:

  1. Root CA — CN <CFSSL_CA_NAME> BaseCA, RSA-4096 by default. CFSSL_CA_NAME must be set in .env (e.g. localmaeher in example_env.sh).
  2. Intermediate CA — CN <CFSSL_CA_NAME>, signed by the root with the intermediate_ca profile (max_path_len: 0, so no deeper CAs can exist).
  3. OCSP signer — CN <CFSSL_CA_NAME> OCSP, issued by the intermediate with the ocsp profile.

All private keys and the SQLite certificate database (certstore_development.db, migrated with goose on every start) stay on the cfssl_data volume. The public halves are exported to the shared ca_public volume as root_ca.pem, intermediate_ca.pem and ca_chain.pem — every other service mounts ca_public read-mostly to trust the deployment CA.

Signing lifetimes come from the x-cfssl_env anchor in docker-compose.yml: CFSSL_CA_EXPIRY defaults to 2016h (12 weeks) for both CA certificates and CFSSL_SIGN_DEFAULT_EXPIRY to 1008h (6 weeks) for leaf certificates. The README's production example raises both to 8800h (about a year) — with the defaults, a long-lived deployment's CA simply expires. Every issued certificate embeds a public ocsp_url (https://<domain>:443/ca/ocsp) and crl_url (https://<domain>:443/ca/crl/crl.pem) pointing back at the deployment's nginx.

The signing config defines five profiles: client (digital signature, key encipherment, client auth — the one used for end users), server, peer, ocsp and intermediate_ca.

How rasenmaeher-api issues client certificates

rmapi talks to this plane through three environment variables in the compose file: RM_CFSSL_HOST: "http://cfssl" (port 8888), RM_OCSPREST_HOST: "http://ocsprest" (port 8887) and RM_OCSCP_RESPONDER (sic — the env var name carries a typo) set to the public OCSP URL. The API's cert layer is pluggable (rasenmaeher_api/cert/backend.py); the default backend is CFSSL, and the compose stack does not override it. The alternative cert_manager backend in the same codebase is what the Kubernetes port uses.

When a person is created (Person.create_with_cert in db/people.py):

  • The callsign becomes the certificate CN. If the enrollee supplies their own CSR, its CN must equal the callsign or the request is rejected; otherwise rmapi generates the keypair and CSR itself with subject {"CN": callsign}.
  • Callsigns that collide with product CNs (tak.<domain> etc.) are refused outright.
  • The CSR is POSTed to ocsprest at /api/v1/csr/sign with profile: "client"; ocsprest drives the cfssl CLI and returns the signed PEM plus bundle.
  • Keys and certificates are stored under /data/persistent/private/people/<uuid>/ on the rmapi_data volume, and can be handed to the user as a PKCS#12 bundle for import into browsers and TAK clients.

Products get service certificates from the same CA by a different route: miniwerk embeds a one-time, 24-hour CSR JWT (subject <product>.<domain>) in each product's kraftwerk-init.json manifest, and the product's kw_product_init bootstrap uses it to have rmapi sign a certificate with CN <product>.<domain>. rmapi pins that CN (the certcn field in its own manifest) when it calls the product's integration API over mTLS.

The full enrollment path, end to end:

sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant rmapi
    participant ocsprest
    participant cfssl
    participant nginx
    participant ocsp

    User->>rmapi: Enroll with callsign on the base domain
    Note over User,rmapi: an admin approves the enrollment (approvecode flow)
    rmapi->>rmapi: Generate keypair and CSR with CN equal to callsign
    rmapi->>ocsprest: POST /api/v1/csr/sign with profile client
    ocsprest->>cfssl: Sign CSR with the intermediate CA
    cfssl-->>ocsprest: Signed certificate PEM
    ocsprest-->>rmapi: Certificate and CA bundle
    rmapi-->>User: Client certificate as PKCS12 download
    User->>nginx: TLS handshake at the mtls subdomain with client cert
    nginx->>ocsp: OCSP query for the leaf certificate
    ocsp-->>nginx: Status good
    alt client certificate verifies
        nginx->>rmapi: Proxy /api with X-ClientCert-DN and X-ClientCert-Serial headers
    else verification fails
        nginx-->>User: 302 to the base domain error page with code mtls_fail
    end

blocks.html:
On the nginx side, the mtls.<domain> server block verifies the presented client certificate against /ca_public/ca_chain.pem and forwards verified requests with X-ClientCert-* headers, from which rmapi reads the callsign — the server-block anatomy is covered in Networking & subdomains.

OCSP and revocation

Unlike the Kubernetes stack, the legacy edge actively enforces revocation. The mtls.<domain> vhost sets ssl_ocsp leaf with ssl_ocsp_responder http://ocsp:8889, so nginx checks the presented client certificate's OCSP status on the internal ocspnet network during the handshake. TAK server likewise runs with TAK_OCSP_ENABLE: "true" in the compose file.

Revocation flows through rmapi: revoke_pem / revoke_serial mark the certificate in CFSSL's database, then ocsprest regenerates the pre-signed OCSP responses (cfssl ocsprefresh) that the ocsp service serves. For external clients, nginx exposes the CA publicly on the base domain: /ca/public/ serves the ca_public files, /ca/ocsp proxies to ocsp:8889, and /ca/crl/ proxies to rmapi's CRL endpoint (/api/v1/utils/crl/) — matching the ocsp_url and crl_url baked into every issued certificate.

miniwerk: Let's Encrypt for the public plane

miniwerk (pvarki/miniwerk:1.8.2-260524-d2.9.0) is a one-shot init service: it runs first, exits, and nearly every other service gates on condition: service_completed_successfully. It does two jobs.

Job 1 — public certificates. It computes the full hostname list — see Networking & subdomains for the subdomain model — and calls certbot certonly --standalone (it binds port 80 itself; the compose file publishes 80:80 on the miniwerk service for the HTTP-01 challenge). All hostnames go into one expanded certificate (--cert-name rasenmaeher, --expand, --keep-until-expiring), which is then copied to the le_certs volume as /le_certs/rasenmaeher/fullchain.pem and privkey.pem.

Consumers of that single certificate: rmnginx (port 443) and productsnginx (ports 4626/4627) as their server certificate, Keycloak (its init script converts the PEMs into the kcserver-keys.jks keystore for its own TLS on 9443), OpenLDAP (LDAPS on 1636), MediaMTX, the TAK containers and Synapse.

Rough edges to know about:

  • MW_LE_TEST defaults to true — a fresh deployment gets Let's Encrypt staging certificates that browsers reject. You must set it to false for production (see example_env.sh).
  • There is no renewal daemon. miniwerk runs once at composition start; certificates renew only when the stack is restarted (certbot's --keep-until-expiring makes restarts cheap). LE account state is bind-mounted to ./le_state on the host.
  • MW_MKCERT=true switches to a locally generated mkcert CA instead of certbot for environments where Let's Encrypt is unreachable; MW_KEYTYPE is set to rsa in the compose file.

Job 2 — product manifests. From the same MW_PRODUCTS list, miniwerk writes the "kraftwerk" manifests into per-product shared volumes (/pvarkishares/<product>): kraftwerk-rasenmaeher-init.json tells rmapi each product's API URL, user URL and expected certificate CN, and each product's kraftwerk-init.json points back at rmapi (base and mTLS URIs) and carries the one-time CSR JWT described above. This is why adding a product to the legacy stack means touching MW_PRODUCTS and re-running miniwerk — DNS names, certificates and service discovery all derive from that one variable.

Contrast with Kubernetes

On the Kubernetes platform (pvarki/opendefence-platform), CFSSL and miniwerk are entirely replaced — none of the containers on this page exist there:

Legacy (this page) Kubernetes replacement
CFSSL root + intermediate, init shell script cert-manager ClusterIssuer chain (selfsigned-issuer → root CA → intermediate-ca-issuer) — see PKI & trust
ca_public volume with ca_chain.pem trust-manager Bundle/ca-bundle synced into every namespace
rmapi → ocsprest /api/v1/csr/sign Same codebase, RM_CERT_BACKEND=cert_manager: rmapi creates cert-manager CertificateRequests (callsign still = CN)
miniwerk + certbot, one expanded LE cert Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 ClusterIssuers in the cloud overlay; no miniwerk
kraftwerk manifests on shared volumes Plain ConfigMaps mounted at /pvarki
ssl_ocsp leaf + ocsp responder, TAK_OCSP_ENABLE "true" OCSP is disabled for now (no responder; TAK_OCSP_ENABLE "false"); the callsign-validity check is the interim revocation enforcement — see Edge mTLS & callsign checks

The last row is an inversion: here the legacy stack is currently stricter than its successor — revoked certificates are refused at the nginx handshake, while the Kubernetes stack relies on a per-request callsign validity lookup instead. The edge-layer mapping (nginx server blocks → Traefik) lives in the Networking & subdomains contrast table.
